title: "Versioning" module (git, data/protocol versioning, DOIs)
context: Cancer researchers routinely lose analysis history through undocumented environments, ad-hoc spreadsheet tracking of protocols, and overwritten data files. Version control for code, data, and protocols is a foundational reproducibility skill that is rarely taught to bench scientists. This module teaches git basics, data/protocol versioning strategies, and DOI-based archiving in plain language, with a runnable container-based exercise and a synthetic or low-risk worked example. Depends on: template-004, container-ci-005.
objective: Author the 'Versioning' module covering git for code, data/protocol versioning strategies, and DOI-based archiving (Zenodo, OSF) following the module template, with 3-6 Bloom-aligned learning objectives, a runnable pinned-container exercise, a worked example or synthetic exercise, checklist/takeaway, formative assessment, and instructor notes; CI green; signed off by Educator and Technical reviewers.
acceptanceCriteria: Module follows the template: 3-6 Bloom-aligned learning objectives, lesson narrative with all assertions cited, runnable pinned-container exercise, worked example or synthetic exercise, checklist/takeaway, formative assessment, and instructor notes.
Teaches git for code versioning (init, commit, branch, tag, remote), data/protocol versioning strategies (version-named files, DVC, OSF versions), and DOI-based archiving via Zenodo and OSF.
Hands-on exercise runs in a pinned container and passes CI (Docker + Apptainer); if a real dataset is used it has a committed PASS gate artifact; otherwise a synthetic dataset is used.
No raw data committed; no biological/clinical conclusion presented as a finding.
All lesson assertions cited; link/citation checker passes in CI.
Reviewed and signed off by Educator reviewer and Technical reviewer; DCO signed off.
resources: The Turing Way — version control chapter (https://the-turing-way.netlify.app/)
Software Carpentry — Version Control with Git (https://swcarpentry.github.io/git-novice/)
output: A complete 'Versioning' module committed to the project repo (lesson, exercise, worked example or synthetic exercise, checklist, assessment, instructor notes) with CI green (Docker + Apptainer) and Educator + Technical reviewer sign-offs.
